Board Important – Karnataka 2nd PUC Blueprint

Chapter-wise weightage, the highest-yield topics, and the exact answers examiners look for in Molecular Basis of Inheritance.
~9–11 marksOne of the highest-weightage chapters in the 2nd PUC Biology paper
1 × 5 MUsually one long answer – lac operon, Meselson-Stahl, Hershey-Chase or DNA fingerprinting
1–2 × 3 MTranscription unit, genetic code features, replication mechanism
2–3 × 2 MNucleoside vs nucleotide, template vs coding strand, capping & tailing
1–2 × 1 MDefinitions and numbers – pitch, base pairs per turn, dystrophin, SNPs
Board Important — Repeated Question Bank
Categorized 1M, 2M, 3M & 5M model answers and value points for the most-repeated board questions.
Board Important — High-Priority Topics Blueprint
Topics ranked by recurring weightage, with the concepts and diagrams examiners expect.

⭐⭐⭐ Top priority – almost always asked

  • Lac operon (5 M) – draw and label i, p, o, z, y, a; explain regulation in the absence of the inducer (repressor binds operator → negative regulation) and in its presence (allolactose inactivates the repressor → transcription proceeds). Name Jacob and Monod, 1961.
  • Meselson-Stahl experiment (5 M) – 15NH4Cl, CsCl density gradient centrifugation, hybrid DNA at 20 min, hybrid + light in equal amounts at 40 min. State clearly that 15N is NOT radioactive.
  • Hershey-Chase experiment (5 M) – 35S labels protein, 32P labels DNA, blending, centrifugation, conclusion that DNA enters the bacterium.
  • Salient features of the Watson-Crick model (5 M) – two antiparallel chains, complementary base pairing with 2 and 3 H-bonds, right-handed coil, pitch 3.4 nm, 10 bp/turn, 20 Å diameter, base stacking.
  • Salient features of the genetic code (5 M) – triplet, unambiguous, degenerate, universal, commaless, AUG dual function, three stop codons.

⭐⭐ High priority – frequently asked

  • DNA fingerprinting methodology (5 M) – Alec Jeffreys, VNTR probes, restriction digestion → electrophoresis → Southern blotting → hybridisation → autoradiography, plus three applications.
  • Salient features of the HGP (5 M) – 3 × 109 bases, ~30,000 genes, dystrophin 2.4 Mb, <2% coding, chromosome 1 (2968) vs Y (231), SNPs at 1.4 million sites.
  • Transcription in eukaryotes (3 M) – three RNA polymerases and hnRNA processing by capping, tailing and splicing.
  • Mechanism of DNA replication (3 M) – origin, replication fork, 5′→3′ polymerisation, leading vs lagging strand, Okazaki fragments, DNA ligase.
  • Griffith's experiment (3 M) – S and R strains, the four injections, and the conclusion (transforming principle, chemical nature unknown).
  • Packaging of DNA (3 M) – the 2.2 m calculation, histone octamer, nucleosome (~200 bp), beads-on-string, NHC proteins.

⭐ Two-mark favourites – learn as clean pairs

  • Nucleoside vs nucleotide · template strand vs coding strand · exon vs intron.
  • Capping vs tailing · leading strand vs lagging strand · euchromatin vs heterochromatin.
  • Inducible vs repressible operon · point mutation vs frameshift mutation · DNA vs RNA.
  • Why DNA is more stable than RNA · why both DNA strands are not transcribed · properties of a genetic material.
  • Translational unit and UTRs · ribozyme (23S rRNA) · adaptor molecule (tRNA).
Answer-writing tip: for every 5-mark experiment, the examiner expects five numbered points – organism/material used, the labelling or treatment, the observation, the control, and the conclusion. Write them as (i)–(v), not as a paragraph.
Never lose these marks: always write the year and the scientists (Griffith 1928, Avery-MacLeod-McCarty 1933–44, Hershey-Chase 1952, Meselson-Stahl 1958, Taylor 1958, Jacob & Monod 1961, HGP 1990–2003).

Board-exam priority list of key diagrams with mark weightage, crucial labels and marking scheme notes.

DNA: The Genetic Material

Fig 5.1 — A Polynucleotide Chain 2 – 3 M ★★☆ High Priority
Label: nitrogenous base, deoxyribose sugar, phosphate, N-glycosidic bond, 3′-5′ phosphodiester bond, free 5′ phosphate and free 3′ -OH.
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.2 — DNA Double Helix (Watson-Crick Model) 3 – 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: antiparallel 5′→3′ and 3′→5′ strands, sugar-phosphate backbone, A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds), pitch 3.4 nm, 10 bp per turn, diameter 20 Å.
View in NCERT PDF →

Packaging of DNA

Fig 5.3 — The Nucleosome 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: histone octamer (8 histone molecules), ~200 bp of DNA wound around it, and the direction of winding. Mention lysine & arginine give the positive charge.
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.4 — ‘Beads-on-String’ Chromatin (EM view) 2 M ★★☆ High Priority
Show nucleosomes as beads on a DNA string, then the chromatin fibre and metaphase chromosome. Mention NHC proteins for higher-order packing.
View in NCERT PDF →

The Search for Genetic Material

Fig 5.5 — Griffith's Transformation Experiment 3 M ★★☆ High Priority
Show all four injections: live S (dies), live R (lives), heat-killed S (lives), live R + heat-killed S (dies, live S recovered).
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.6 — The Hershey-Chase Experiment 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Two parallel tracks: 35S-labelled phages (radioactivity in the supernatant) and 32P-labelled phages (radioactivity in the pellet). Label blending and centrifugation.
View in NCERT PDF →

DNA Replication

Fig 5.7 — Meselson-Stahl Density Gradient Result 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Draw the CsCl tubes at 0, 20 and 40 minutes: heavy band, single hybrid band, then equal hybrid and light bands.
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.8 — The Replication Fork 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: parental strands with polarity, leading strand (continuous), lagging strand with Okazaki fragments, DNA polymerase, and the direction of fork movement.
View in NCERT PDF →

Transcription

Fig 5.9 — Schematic Structure of a Transcription Unit 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: promoter (upstream), structural gene, terminator (downstream), template strand (3′→5′) and coding strand (5′→3′) with polarities marked.
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.10 — hnRNA Processing (Capping, Tailing, Splicing) 3 M ★★☆ High Priority
Show hnRNA with exons and introns, then the 5′ methyl guanosine cap, the 3′ poly-A tail (200–300 residues) and the spliced mature mRNA.
View in NCERT PDF →

Genetic Code & Translation

Fig 5.11 — tRNA, the Adaptor Molecule 2 – 3 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label the clover-leaf form: anticodon loop, amino acid acceptor end (3′ end), and the inverted-L three-dimensional shape.
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.12 — Translation on the Ribosome 3 M ★★☆ High Priority
Label: mRNA with 5′ UTR, start codon, translational unit, stop codon, 3′ UTR; large and small ribosomal subunits; charged tRNA; growing polypeptide.
View in NCERT PDF →

Regulation of Gene Expression

Fig 5.13 — The Lac Operon (ON and OFF states) 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Draw both states. Label i, p, o, z, y and a; the repressor protein on the operator (no lactose) and the inducer-inactivated repressor with RNA polymerase transcribing (with lactose).
View in NCERT PDF →

HGP & DNA Fingerprinting

Fig 5.14 — Steps of Genome Sequencing 3 M ★★☆ High Priority
Flow chart: isolate DNA → fragment → clone in BAC/YAC → amplify in host → automated (Sanger) sequencing → alignment by overlaps → annotation.
View in NCERT PDF →
Fig 5.15 — Schematic of DNA Fingerprinting 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Flow chart with the banding pattern: restriction digestion → gel electrophoresis → Southern blotting → VNTR probe hybridisation → autoradiogram matching a crime-scene sample to individual B, not A.
View in NCERT PDF →

Chapter 5 – Mind Map

One-page visual overview of the whole chapter · pinch or use buttons to zoom
MOLECULAR BASIS OF INHERITANCE
1 · DNA STRUCTURE
Nucleoside (base+sugar, N-glycosidic) → Nucleotide (+phosphate) → 3′-5′ phosphodiester chain
Meischer · Wilkins & Franklin · Watson & Crick · Chargaff
Antiparallel · A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3) · right-handed
Pitch 3.4 nm · 10 bp/turn · 0.34 nm · 20 Å
Central dogma; reverse transcription (Temin & Baltimore, 1970)
2 · PACKAGING
6.6 × 109 bp × 0.34 nm = 2.2 m in a 10−6 m nucleus
Prokaryote: nucleoid, loops, basic non-histone proteins
Eukaryote: histone octamer (lysine, arginine) → nucleosome (~200 bp)
Beads-on-string → chromatin fibre (NHC) → chromosome
Euchromatin (active) vs heterochromatin (inactive)
3 · SEARCH FOR GENETIC MATERIAL
Griffith 1928 → transforming principle (S vs R strain)
Avery, MacLeod & McCarty → DNase abolishes transformation
Hershey & Chase 1952 → 32P in, 35S out
Properties: replicate · stable · mutable · expressible
DNA vs RNA; RNA evolved first (TMV, Qβ)
4 · REPLICATION
Semi-conservative (Watson & Crick 1953), S phase
Meselson & Stahl 1958: 15N, CsCl gradient, hybrid → hybrid+light
Taylor 1958: Vicia faba, radioactive thymidine
Origin · fork · 5′→3′ only · leading vs lagging
Okazaki fragments + ligase · ~2000 bp/sec in E. coli
5 · TRANSCRIPTION
Promoter – structural gene – terminator
Template (3′→5′) vs coding strand (misnomer)
Cistron · monocistronic/split vs polycistronic · exon/intron
mRNA, tRNA, rRNA · sigma (start), rho (stop)
Pol I / II / III · capping, tailing, splicing
6 · GENETIC CODE & tRNA
Gamow 43 = 64 · Khorana, Nirenberg, Ochoa
Triplet · unambiguous · degenerate · universal · commaless
AUG start/Met · UAA, UAG, UGA stop
Exceptions: ciliates, human mitochondria
Point (sickle-cell) vs frameshift · tRNA = adaptor
7 · TRANSLATION & REGULATION
Activation → charging → initiation → elongation → termination
23S rRNA = ribozyme · translational unit & UTRs
Operon = polycistronic + promoter + regulatory genes
Lac (inducible, catabolic): i, p, o, z, y, a – Jacob & Monod 1961
Trp (repressible, anabolic): aporepressor + tryptophan corepressor
8 · HGP & DNA FINGERPRINTING
1990–2003 · DOE + NIH + Wellcome Trust · ELSI
ESTs vs sequence annotation · BAC/YAC · Sanger
3 × 109 bases · ~30,000 genes · <2% coding
Dystrophin 2.4 Mb · chr 1 = 2968, Y = 231 · SNPs 1.4 million
Jeffreys · VNTR · digest → electrophoresis → Southern blot → autoradiography
Tip: on mobile, rotate to landscape or use the zoom buttons; scroll inside the frame to pan across the map.
